correctness.rationale: The frozen RESULT.md defines A_k(n) as the minimum circumscribing n-gon area and the weighted secant at 6 for all integer 3<=m<6<n. The cited Lángi–Wang Lemma 3.7 formulas and monotonicity reduce each fixed k to finite comparisons through n=2k. For k=4,5,7, explicit symbolic triples A(5)+A(7)=2A(6) with strict spacing make strictly concave powers 0<alpha<1 and log fail, while Dowker convexity proves all alpha>=1. For other k<=15, the independently reproduced full 426 strict logarithmic comparisons, not a partial sample, are the finite component of the proof. For all k>=16, the analytic log convexity of d(x)=x tan(pi/x), the exact universal disk comparison d(n)<=A_k(n)<=sec(pi/(2k))^2 d(n), and the rational cutoff d(5)d(7)/d(6)^2>51/50>sec(pi/32)^4 cover infinitely many k. Weighted AM-GM promotes log to every positive power; the Lángi–Wang log-honeycomb implication transfers the outcome to normal convex unit-area tilings. k=2,3 follow from A(n)=A(6) for n>=6. Independent mpmath 65-digit comparison corroborated 426 finite inequalities and the disk cutoff, with no claim that numerical tests prove the infinite part.
residual_risks: Checker finite arithmetic is not a substitute for k>=16 log-convexity or published tiling implication.
A claim of tiling nonoptimality at exceptional k would be invalid and is not made.
